correctness.rationale: For a shell of radius t the restricted ultrametric has diameter at most t, and a last-common-ancestor height of (r-t)d(x,y)/2 above the leaves produces the required same-shell path cost, with a stem if the graft height L(t) exceeds the dendrogram height. Along the trunk H is strictly increasing. F=H+L and H-L=2rt, so pairs at distinct interior radii t<s give F(s)-2rt, exactly (r-s)s+2r(s-t); the equality d(x,y)=s follows from the strong triangle inequality in both directions. At the root the cost is F(t), and with an outside endpoint it is 2r(r-t) or 2r^2 from the root; all outside sites map to the same vertex. This accounts for the cutoff equality d(m,x)=r, singleton shells and the degenerate pair costs. The cut formula is a lower bound by conservation on every edge, and it is attained by decomposing the unique signed net tree flow into transport paths plus stationary mass. Any plan on the quotient tree vertices lifts by distributing each incoming and outgoing amount according to the original marginal masses in each fiber. Maximizing over centers then gives the stated metric without interchanging transport and maximization. The stated line counterexample has distinct largest and second-largest four-point sums (10 and 9).
residual_risks: The exact proof, not the numerical LP tolerance, establishes the result for arbitrary weights and finite ultrametric sizes. No extension to the different pointwise modified cost or to arbitrary metric spaces is implied.

value.rationale: The result converts a stability-related localized metric defined via a family of transport optimizations into weighted sums of observable mass imbalances in a natural hierarchical class. For a fixed support and scale the trees depend only on the metric and can be reused for arbitrary measure comparisons, which replaces an entire transport LP at each center by a subtree pass. The obstruction on the ordinary four-point line shows this representation is not merely a restatement for all finite inputs.
residual_risks: No claim is made about optimal preprocessing time, general metrics, or stronger nerve-map stability bounds.
